Beyond Miami

Bring the rest of the country to Miami

You asked the right question on our call: patients in states without accessible stem cell therapy already travel, out of state or out of the country, for treatment. Florida's regulatory environment gives Miami a real first mover advantage domestically. We ran the actual numbers against the keyword list you sent over. Of 451 keywords audited, 341 are real opportunity for STEMS Health once we strip out the roughly quarter of the list that's tied to a specific overseas clinic's brand names and destination specific searches, that's a different clinic's competitive set, not yours. What's left is 144,870 searches a month of on-label opportunity.

Two things we deliberately left out. About 11,400 searches a month are overseas clinic brand names and destination specific queries (CPI, R3, CHIPSA and similar), a different clinic's competitors, not yours to chase. About 10,900 more span autism, MS, diabetes, COPD, and similar conditions we didn't see listed anywhere on your site. We don't build pages claiming to treat conditions you don't treat, that's exactly what the FTC has gone after stem cell clinics for. If your physicians do treat any of these, say so and we'll add them properly, reviewed and sourced like everything else.

Looking at your own site turned up gaps the keyword list doesn't cover at all yet: elbow, ankle and foot, wrist and hand pain, bursitis, tendinitis, ligament and muscle tears, women's health and hormonal support, peptide therapy, athletic recovery and longevity, stem cell banking, the VIA disc procedure, and regenerative aesthetics. Worth a second keyword pull on those specifically before we lock the page map, peptides especially, since that's the same 0% visibility gap we already found locally.

Rough page count once the gaps are filled: somewhere around 55 to 65 pages, phased over two to three quarters. Worth scoping in detail on our next call, with both of you in the room. You mentioned PR is already underway on your side too, we'd tie that directly into this content plan so a press placement and a well built page reinforce the same authority signal.

Content Production Model

One human template, then AI does the rest, except where it can't

Not every page gets made the same way. Location pages scale. Medical claims don't.

Step 1

One city, written by hand

We write the full template page for a single city by hand: structure, tone, local specifics, all of it. That becomes the pattern every other page follows.

Step 2

AI scales the rest

Every other city and state page is generated from that template with its own real details filled in, not a copy with the name swapped out.

Physician authored

Condition pages come from your side

Any page making a medical claim, what a condition is, what the evidence shows, who's a candidate, gets written by STEMS Health's own doctors or writers. That's the source content.

Reused, not rewritten

One condition page, every location

Once your physicians write the master version of a condition page, we localize it across every city and state page that needs it, keeping the medical content exactly as your team wrote it.

Two ways to get the medical content written: your doctors or in house writers draft it, and it doubles as the source content our AI localizes from, at no cost to you. Or we write it for you at $200 an article. Either way, nothing claiming a medical outcome goes out the door without a name and credentials behind it.
